story: In October 1989, NASA launched the Galileo spacecraft aboard Space Shuttle Atlantis after years of delays and anti-nuclear lawsuits over its plutonium power source. To reach Jupiter, Galileo executed a complex trajectory, swinging past Venus and Earth for gravity assists. Along the way, it captured historic images of asteroids Gaspra and Ida and observed Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 crashing into Jupiter. Disaster struck in deep space when Galileo's main high-gain antenna failed to unfold, threatening the mission. Engineers rescued the project by sending a software overhaul across millions of miles to compress data so the backup low-gain antenna could function. Arriving at Jupiter in 1995, Galileo discovered active volcanoes on Io and evidence of a liquid ocean beneath Europa's ice. Finally, on September 21, 2003, NASA deliberately plunged Galileo into Jupiter's atmosphere to destroy it, ensuring Earth microbes would never contaminate Europa's potential life.
angle: When Galileo's main high-gain antenna jammed in deep space, engineers salvaged the mission by beaming a complete software overhaul across hundreds of millions of miles.

claims.claim: The Galileo space mission was named in honor of the 17th-century Italian astronomer Galileo Galilei.
Galileo's launch was delayed for years following the 1986 Space Shuttle Challenger disaster.
Anti-nuclear groups filed legal action seeking to stop Galileo's launch due to safety concerns over radioactive plutonium.
The spacecraft was powered by Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generators using plutonium-238 because solar power was impractical at Jupiter.
Galileo was launched into space aboard Space Shuttle Atlantis in October 1989.
The spacecraft utilized gravity assist flybys of Venus and Earth to gain necessary momentum toward Jupiter.
Galileo performed flybys and photographed the asteroids Gaspra and Ida during its journey.
Galileo provided direct observations of Comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 impacting Jupiter in July 1994.
Galileo's primary high-gain antenna failed to deploy properly in deep space, forcing reliance on its slower low-gain antenna.
Galileo reached Jupiter and entered orbit around the planet in December 1995.
Galileo discovered evidence of a deep, salty ocean beneath the frozen surface of Jupiter's moon Europa.
Galileo observed massive volcanic activity and fire fountains erupting on Jupiter's moon Io.
Galileo was intentionally sent into Jupiter's atmosphere to disintegrate on September 21, 2003.
NASA deliberately destroyed Galileo in Jupiter's atmosphere to prevent accidental biological contamination of Europa by Earth microbes.

disputed: Health risks and potential cancer deaths in the event of an accidental reentry explosion: Anti-nuclear groups estimated thousands of fatal cancers, an interagency evaluation panel estimated up to 2,000 deaths, while NASA estimated zero additional deaths. A script should attribute these opposing perspectives if mentioned.
